video.title: Cicerone Study: Cicerone Off-Flavor Tasting Kit - Ep. #1279

keyPoints.line: diacetyl: rushed beer or dirty lines.

read.bigIdea: Five flaws every beer pro should spot.
read.where: Cicerone’s Certified Cicerone tasting exam spikes beers with five: **acetaldehyde** (green apple, latex paint; beer pulled off the yeast too early), **DMS** (cooked corn, cabbage; a weak or covered boil), **diacetyl** (butter, butterscotch; rushed fermentation or dirty draft lines), **lightstruck** (skunky; light) and **trans-2-nonenal** (wet cardboard, paper; oxidation). A light DMS note is allowed in some pale lagers, a little diacetyl in some English and Czech beers.
read.mixup: Some people can’t smell diacetyl at all. If a guest says butter, believe them.

keyPoints.line: right in Weizen, a fault elsewhere.
a whiff OK in some German lagers.

read.where: **Banana** (isoamyl acetate) is the signature of Weissbier; in other styles strong banana is a **fault** from fermenting too warm. **Sulfur**: rotten egg or struck match from yeast, usually gone by packaging; a faint whiff is normal in some German lagers and Kölsch. **Solvent** and **hot alcohol** (nail polish, burning) come from fermenting too warm or too little yeast; a little warmth is normal in barleywine.
read.mixup: Banana in a pilsner is a fault. Banana in a Hefeweizen is the point.

video.title: Contamination (Infection) - Beer sensory characteristics, causes and control factors

keyPoints.line: bacteria, unless the style is sour.

read.where: **Medicinal** (plastic, Band-Aid) is **chlorophenol**: chlorine from tap water or sanitizer reacting with the beer. **Metallic** (coins, blood, ink) comes from iron or worn equipment. **Butyric** acid (baby vomit, rancid butter) points to bacteria and poor hygiene. **Lactic** (yogurt) and **acetic** (vinegar) sourness are right in lambic, Flanders and Berliner weisse; anywhere else they mean bacteria, and on draft, **dirty lines**.
read.mixup: A sour IPA on purpose is fine. An IPA that’s gone sour on draft isn’t.

video.title: Papery (Trans-2-nonenal) - Beer sensory characteristics, causes and control factors

read.bigIdea: How age and old hops show.
read.where: **Oxidation** shows as **cardboard** and paper in pale, light beers; in strong, dark beers it turns **sherry**-like (dried fruit, almond), which can add complexity to barleywine. **Isovaleric** acid (aged cheese, **sweaty socks**) usually means **old, badly stored hops**. **Mercaptans** are tropical in some new hops at low levels, but onion, garlic or **burnt rubber** when high. **Astringency** is puckering, like over-steeped tea: tannin from grain husks or heavy hopping.
read.mixup: Sherry notes in a 10-year-old barleywine can be good. In a pale lager, any oxidation is a fault.
